:::{#thm-kl-divergence-discrete}
#### KL divergence of two mass functions

Let $p$ and $q$ be [probability mass functions](random-variables.qmd#def-pmf) on $\set{1, \ldots, K}$,
with $p_k$ and $q_k$ the probabilities of outcome $k$,
and suppose $q_k > 0$ whenever $p_k > 0$.
Then the [KL divergence](#def-kl-divergence) is

$$\kldivf{p}{q} = \sumto{k}{K} p_k \log \frac{p_k}{q_k}.$$

A term with $p_k = 0$ is taken to be $0$.

:::

::: proof

By [the discrete formula for cross-entropy](#thm-cross-entropy-discrete),

$$
\ba
\kldivf{p}{q}
&= \crossentropyf{p}{q} - \crossentropyf{p}{p} && \text{(definition)} \\
&= -\sumto{k}{K} p_k \log q_k + \sumto{k}{K} p_k \log p_k && \text{(discrete formula, twice)} \\
&= \sumto{k}{K} p_k \paren{\log p_k - \log q_k} && \text{(combine the sums)} \\
&= \sumto{k}{K} p_k \log \frac{p_k}{q_k}. && \text{(difference of logarithms)}
\ea
$$

:::
